item.title: Charli XCX ‘Music, Fashion, Film’ Album Review
item.description: How does one follow a pop album that became a cultural juggernaut? On “Music, Fashion, Film,” Charli XCX embraces, and even glorifies, the slapdash.
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Zoladz

item.title: How Conor Oberst Survived Teenage Rock Stardom
item.description: The singer-songwriter opens up about life as a niche icon for more than 30 years, the personal struggles that nearly killed him and trying to write political music under President Trump.
item.dc:creator: Joe Coscarelli, Jon Caramanica and Jason Nocito
item.media:credit: Jason Nocito for The New York Times

item.title: An A.I. Music F.A.Q.: Can I Remix Madonna? Is This All Legal?
item.description: Advances in A.I. are making it possible to create all kinds of music from scratch, but they also raise questions about what is legal and who will actually listen.
item.dc:creator: Ben Sisario

item.title: The Devotion of Willow Smith
item.description: The daughter of a Hollywood power couple, she has gone above and beyond to prove herself. Virtuosity and spiritual aspirations fill her latest, “The Thread.”
item.dc:creator: Jon Pareles

item.title: Overlooked No More: Barbara Rubin, Teenage Filmmaker at the Heart of New York’s Underground
item.description: She made the landmark underground film “Christmas on Earth,” and helped bring together artists like Andy Warhol, Allen Ginsberg and Bob Dylan.
item.dc:creator: J. Hoberman
item.media:credit: Fred W. McDarrah/The New York Historical, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Rubin in 1964. She was known for connecting important figures of New York’s avant-garde movement with one another.

item.title: Victoria Monét, Sam Smith: Songs to Know This Week
item.description: Victoria Monét goes girl-group, Sam Smith gets a choral assist, and Chad Hugo re-emerges.
item.dc:creator: Jon Pareles

item.title: Freddy Cannon, Rocker Who Sang ‘Palisades Park,’ Dies at 89
item.description: Known as Boom Boom, he recorded a string of hits in the 1950s and ’60s, including “Tallahassee Lassie,” which began as a poem by his mother.
item.dc:creator: Richard Sandomir
item.media:description: Freddy Cannon in 1963. He rose to stardom in an era teeming with clean-cut teen idols like Fabian, Frankie Avalon and Bobby Rydell.

item.title: D4vd Had Sexual Relationship With Teenager, Detective Testifies in Murder Case
item.description: The testimony came on the fourth day of the singer’s preliminary hearing. He is accused of fatally stabbing Celeste Rivas Hernandez, 14, and dismembering her body.
item.dc:creator: Matt Stevens
item.media:description: Months after Celeste Rivas Hernandez’s body was discovered in September, D4vd was arrested and charged with murder.

item.title: Chris Brown Pleads Guilty to Affray Charge in London Nightclub Assault Case
item.description: The R&B star pleaded guilty to a charge of affray after being accused of attacking a producer in 2023. He is set to be sentenced in October.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Wolfe
item.media:description: Chris Brown gives an autograph as he leaves Southwark Crown Court in London on Friday.

item.title: Doreen Broadnax, Famous (as Sparky D) for ’80s Rap Battle, Dies at 61
item.description: Tossing verbal grenades back and forth with Roxanne Shanté, she helped establish a lasting hip-hop truism: Bad blood is good business.
item.dc:creator: Alex Williams
item.media:description: Doreen Broadnax in 1988, after the end of the so-called Roxanne Wars, one of the first rap battles.

item.title: Marlboro Music: Where Artists Have Time to Chase Perfection
item.description: The Marlboro Music festival, now in its 75th summer, allows artists to practice for however long they’d like, with no pressure to perform.
item.dc:creator: David Weininger
item.media:credit: Graham Dickie for The New York Times
item.media:description: Visitors to the Marlboro Music Festival are greeted by this sign, one of many playful elements on its campus.

item.title: Kenneth Blume Steps Out of Kenny Beats’s Shadow
item.description: The hitmaker formerly known as Kenny Beats was behind breakthrough albums for Geese, Vince Staples, Idles and Fcukers. On a new solo project, he turns his focus inward.
item.dc:creator: Reggie Ugwu
item.media:credit: Morganne Boulden for The New York Times
item.media:description: Blume wrote lyrics for his new solo album after an emotionally battering period of caring for his ill father. “The music feels like a safe place to get everything I want to say out,” he said.

item.title: Former Conductor to Plead Guilty in Child Sex Abuse Imagery Case
item.description: Julian Wachner, the former music director at Trinity Church in New York, faces up to 10 years in prison after reaching a plea deal.
item.dc:creator: Derrick Bryson Taylor
item.media:credit: Vincent Tullo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Julian Wachner directed the music program for Trinity Church in New York until his ouster in 2022.

item.title: Plas Johnson, Saxophonist Behind ‘The Pink Panther,’ Dies at 94
item.description: His recording for the theme song, written by Henry Mancini, included a solo improvised in the studio. He also backed Frank Sinatra and Barbra Streisand.
item.dc:creator: Matt Schudel

item.title: Hot, Uncomfortable, Transcendent: Why We Can’t Quit Opera at Bayreuth
item.description: The Bayreuth Festival, where Wagner’s operas have been performed for 150 years, is inconvenient and unpleasant. Why does it have such a hold on us?
item.dc:creator: Joshua Barone

item.title: Madison Square Garden Sues Wired Magazine Over L.G.B.T.Q. Tracking Report
item.description: The Manhattan venue claims a July article from the technology magazine falsely implied that it tracked information about some celebrities’ sexual orientation for “discriminatory purposes.”
item.dc:creator: John S.W. MacDonald and Mack Liederman

item.media:description: Wired reported in a July 9 article that the venue maintained a talent database containing information about the gender identity and sexual orientation of some V.I.P. guests.
